issues.body: `term_to_ntriples` appends `TermRef.direction` verbatim after `--`. `TermRef` is public and deserializable, and form descriptions are intended for JSON consumers, so a returned form can be modified or reconstructed with a direction such as `rtl . } INSERT DATA { <...> <...> <...> . } #`. Passing that form to `to_sparql_update` incorporates the payload as SPARQL syntax rather than an RDF literal direction. RDF 1.2 permits only `ltr` or `rtl`; the write path must fail closed instead of trusting the struct field.
issues.fix_hint: Validate direction as exactly `ltr` or `rtl` before serialization (and preferably validate the associated language tag as well). Change serialization/update construction to return an error for invalid term metadata, or otherwise exclude invalid changes; add a test that mutates/deserializes an invalid direction containing SPARQL punctuation and proves no executable update is produced.
issues.title: Unvalidated base direction permits SPARQL injection

issues.body: The test and public documentation state that without `computed` a `sh:values` field has an EMPTY value vector, but the assertion only checks that the vector is not exactly `["stale"]`. Any arbitrary non-stale value, including an incorrectly evaluated or leaked value, passes. Because this test also runs with `computed` enabled, it cannot express the two feature-state expectations as written.
issues.fix_hint: Under `#[cfg(not(feature = "computed"))]`, assert `computed.values.is_empty()`. Under `#[cfg(feature = "computed")]`, assert the expected computed value (for this fixture, `Bob`) while still asserting that `stale` is absent.
issues.title: Default-feature computed-field test does not prove values are empty

verdict.summary: The RDF 1.2 direction support is not safe on the public write path: a caller-controlled `TermRef.direction` is interpolated into SPARQL without validation or escaping. This can turn a form edit into additional SPARQL syntax. The computed-field implementation itself is feature-gated and avoids asserted-value fallback, but its default-state acceptance test does not actually assert the documented empty-values invariant.
